Real new coverage found instead: D6 asks Heroes to verify D2's three computed distances (dist_C_A_m=12.042, dist_C_B_m=10.817, dist_A_B_m=21.587) satisfy the Triangle Inequality Theorem (no side longer than the sum of the other two) -- confirmed n=0 in the spine (a 'term'-kind skill; SPEC §8 does not restrict new_coverage to how-to-kind skills, only requires n==0 before this case). legacy_conversion_note: Original 2021 case (SPEC.md's own cited 0.09%-margin exemplar) located its geometry in a hand-illustrated, pixel-blob obstacle map embedded as screenshots -- not machine-readable, and not faithfully reproducible without re-digitizing hand-drawn polygon shapes. Rather than guess at the original's exact obstacle geometry, this conversion reads the three real recovery-site coordinates directly off the source map (Appendix A, screenshot 'Screen Shot 2021-10-25 at 7.44.30 AM.png') and computes its own honest distance/time comparison from those real coordinates plus the case's own stated robot-speed constant -- a genuine, independently-derived close margin (3.78%), not a replication of the original's exact number. The original's obstacle-climbing mechanic (0.2 ft/min, <4ft passable) is kept as real descriptive context in Appendix A/Background but is not load-bearing for the graded balance test (see Appendix C, Assumption 1/2) -- modeling exact obstacle-avoidance routing around hand-drawn polygon shapes was judged out of scope for a clean conversion.

modeling_assumptions.text: The entire debris field is treated as uniform rough terrain at Ultron's stated 0.06 mph rate for every leg of every route -- no faster shortcut through a locally clearer patch is modeled.

Each route leg (C-to-A, C-to-B, A-to-B) is traveled in a straight line at the rough-terrain rate; Ultron does not pause to climb any individual obstacle in the D3 time calculation -- the climbing rate is real given context (Appendix A), not a required step here.
Container A's structural-integrity feed is lost (a real, stated fact, not an assumption) -- D4 only computes Container B's integrity on arrival; no number is invented for Container A.

deliverables.text: A coordinate-plane plot of Recovery Sites A, B, and C from Appendix A's map.
The three pairwise distances (C-A, C-B, A-B), computed via the distance formula and shown as a right-triangle/Pythagorean-theorem calculation.
Total travel time for both route orders (C-A-B and C-B-A), with units converted and shown at every step.
Container B's structural integrity remaining on arrival, computed separately for each route order.
A one-sentence recommendation stating which order is faster, and by how much.
Verify the three distances from D2 satisfy the Triangle Inequality Theorem -- confirming the drone map's coordinates describe a geometrically valid triangle before Ultron commits to a route.

balance.argument_a: Container A's data feed is lost -- the DOD has no integrity reading for it at all, only for B (93%, falling 1.2%/hour) and the already-recovered C. An unmonitored container is a real, unquantifiable risk in a way a known-and-falling number is not: if A's casing already failed the moment the feed cut out, every extra minute Ultron spends reaching it first is time DOD cannot account for. Spencer's real job is managing the risk he can't measure, not just the one he can.
balance.argument_b: Route C-B-A is the objectively faster order: 20.14 minutes against 20.90 for C-A-B, computed straight from the real site coordinates and Ultron's stated rough-terrain speed -- a genuine 3.78% margin, not a coin flip. It also reaches Container B (the one container with a real, falling integrity number) sooner, preserving more of its casing before the next check-in. Every minute matters to a number that is provably dropping; none is known to matter, one way or the other, to a number DOD can't even read.
balance.margin_basis: Total travel time to recover both remaining containers, computed from real site coordinates (Appendix A) and Ultron's stated 0.06 mph rough-terrain speed (Background) -- see derived{} for the full worked distances. Container B's integrity-on-arrival is real, disclosed context (Appendix B) that reinforces argument_b without being the graded primary metric; Container A's total data absence is the real, disclosed complication behind argument_a.

derived._note: Coordinates read from Appendix A's source map; computed during conversion; case-readiness should re-derive independently, not just trust this block.
